attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The bridge is valid, but its source obligation is not barely nontrivial in the original SAT length; it already asks for m^{omega(1)} SAT lower bounds.
steps: Fix a valid length N_m and define H_g by copying the first m input bits into the SAT_m instance; invalid lengths are not part of the source lower-bound claim.
If SAT_m has a circuit of size m^c, wire the first m inputs into it and ignore all padding bits, giving an H_g circuit of size m^c+O(m).
If H_g at N_m has a circuit of size s, restrict the padding bits to constants; the resulting m-input circuit decides SAT_m with size s+O(1).
Substitute N_m=(m+1)^{g(m+1)}. A barely superlinear bound in N is a superpolynomial SAT lower bound when g is unbounded.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: No P != NP proof follows because the unproved source premise already implies NP not subset P/poly through the restriction inequality.

assumptions: C_n(f) denotes minimum fan-in-two Boolean circuit size for the n-bit slice.
The valid-length sequence is injective and g is unbounded on the claimed lower-bound subsequence.
On length N_m, H_g depends only on the first m input bits and ignores padding bits.
The source claim is i.o. C_{N_m}(H_g)>N_m^{1+eps}; invalid lengths are excluded.
definitions: source object: H_g is a projection-padded SAT language with valid lengths N_m=(m+1)^{g(m+1)} and fan-in-two Boolean circuit lower bounds on those slices.
target object: SAT_m against nonuniform fan-in-two Boolean circuits SIZE(m^c), with target consequence NP not subset P/poly.
controlled interface: contrapositive projection from a target SAT circuit family to a valid-length H_g circuit family, using only length-dependent wiring.
target-preserving condition: g(m)->infty on the lower-bound subsequence, and the H_g lower bound is asserted only at valid lengths N_m.

candidate_lemmas.statement: For projection-padded SAT carrier H_g at valid lengths N_m=(m+1)^{g(m+1)}, C(H_g|_{N_m}) is sandwiched by C(SAT_m) up to O(m). Thus an i.o. N^{1+eps} lower bound is an i.o. SAT lower bound m^{(1+eps)g(m+1)}, so unbounded g gives NP not subset P/poly but no weak-source magnification.

control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if a named source model yields N^{1+eps} lower bounds transferring to SAT not in SIZE(n^c) without projection demagnification.

dependency_updates.description: Sparse projection padding is a threshold reparameterization, not genuine magnification from a weak original-length bound.
The source model must be a valid-length circuit lower bound for H_g; all-length claims are invalidated by constant off-carrier slices.
If the source premise holds i.o. with unbounded g, the sandwich gives SAT not in SIZE(m^c) for every c, hence NP not subset P/poly.
A large constructive property proving the H_g lower bound would be natural; only a specific non-natural proof remains outside the known barrier's scope.

falsifiers: falsifier: if the lower bound is asserted on all lengths, invalid lengths are constant slices and the statement becomes false.
falsifier: if the encoding is not a projection and needs an Omega(N) decoder, the O(N) floor collapses the N^{1+eps} threshold.
falsifier: if g is bounded on the lower-bound subsequence, the consequence excludes only finitely many SAT exponents.
falsifier: a large constructive proof property would meet the natural-proofs obstruction; this route needs a specific non-natural lower-bound argument.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing inference is P0 not p-bounded implies no Cook-Reckhow proof system is p-bounded. This is exactly a p-optimality or universal-system lower-bound obligation, not a barrier slogan.
steps: Start with a claimed source lower bound s_EF(tau_n)>|tau_n|^{omega(1)} for an explicit tautology family.
Translate the desired target through the standard interface: NP=coNP iff some Cook-Reckhow proof system is polynomially bounded for all tautologies.
Observe that the EF lower bound proves only that EF is not polynomially bounded on tau_n.
Try to infer that no Cook-Reckhow system is polynomially bounded; this requires EF p-simulating every Cook-Reckhow system or a universal lower bound over all systems.
Construct P_tau by adding tau_n as uniformly checkable axiom instances to P0. P_tau remains a valid Cook-Reckhow system and gives tau_n short proofs.
Therefore the fixed-family, fixed-system lower bound is extension-fragile and cannot be the target-preserving bridge to NP != coNP.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation quarantines an invalid bridge. It does not prove NP != coNP or P != NP; it only identifies the formal target-preservation condition a proof-complexity route must satisfy.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: proof-complexity target-preservation audit

assumptions: P0 is sound, complete for TAUT, and polynomial-time verifiable.
The family tau_n is uniformly constructible and each tau_n is a tautology.
p-simulation means polynomial-time translation with polynomial proof-length overhead.
No p-optimality theorem for EF, Frege, or another named P0 is assumed for free.
definitions: source object: a fixed Cook-Reckhow proof system P0 and an explicit tautology family tau_n with claimed proof-size lower bound s_{P0}(tau_n)>|tau_n|^{omega(1)}.
target object: NP != coNP as the proof-complexity target; this would imply P != NP, but it is stronger and must not be confused with the main conjecture itself.
controlled interface: the Cook-Reckhow verifier V_P(pi,phi), proof length s_P(phi), and the p-simulation preorder between proof systems.

target-preserving condition: P0 must p-simulate every polynomial-time Cook-Reckhow proof system, or the lower bound must quantify over every such system; otherwise fixed-system specificity leaks the target.

equations.label: proof_length
equations.valid_when: Valid when P is a sound and complete Cook-Reckhow propositional proof system with polynomial-time verifier.

equations.label: cr_equivalence
equations.valid_when: Valid when proof systems range over all Cook-Reckhow systems and TAUT is the coNP-complete language.

equations.label: universal_lb_bridge
equations.valid_when: Applies when the lower bound quantifies over every polynomial-time verifiable proof system, not just one calculus.

equations.label: p_optimal_bridge
equations.latex: [(P_0\ \text{p-simulates all}\ P\in CR)\wedge(\forall c)(\exists n)\ s_{P_0}(\tau_n)>|\tau_n|^c]\Rightarrow \mathrm{NP}\ne\mathrm{coNP}
equations.valid_when: Requires the target-preserving universal simulation hypothesis and an infinite uniformly constructible tautology family.

equations.label: extension_falsifier_system
equations.valid_when: Valid when tau_n is uniformly constructible and each tau_n is already known to be a tautology.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a route states EF lower bounds imply P != NP without proving EF p-optimality or universal Cook-Reckhow lower bounds, the tailored system P_tau is a falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Bridge-refutation lemma: it certifies a fixed-system proof lower bound as route-level progress but not a valid transfer to P != NP.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A superpolynomial lower bound for a fixed Cook-Reckhow proof system P0, such as EF or Frege, is not a valid bridge to P != NP unless the route supplies universal p-simulation by P0 or proves lower bounds for every Cook-Reckhow system. The lower bound only refutes P0-p-boundedness; the target NP != coNP requires absence of all p-bounded proof systems.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if the next proposal still proves lower bounds only for one named proof system without p-optimality or universal quantification over Cook-Reckhow systems.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if it proves a universal Cook-Reckhow lower bound, proves the relevant p-optimality theorem, or explicitly downgrades the target to non-p-boundedness of a named proof system.
control_decision.reason: The route loses target preservation through proof-system specificity and implicit nonuniform axiom leakage.

dependency_updates.description: Not the primary obstruction in this cycle; the proof-system verifier is syntactic, but target transfer already fails before oracle behavior matters.
Not the primary obstruction; a proof-length lower bound need not define a large constructive property of truth tables, but non-naturalness does not repair fixed-system leakage.
Not the primary obstruction; even a nonalgebrizing EF lower bound would still need universal Cook-Reckhow target preservation.
Fixed-system lower bounds are quarantined as non-target-preserving unless upgraded to universal Cook-Reckhow lower bounds or p-optimal-system lower bounds.

falsifiers: falsifier: the valid Cook-Reckhow extension P_tau gives O(log n)-size proofs of the allegedly hard family tau_n while preserving soundness and completeness.
falsifier: a route whose theorem mentions only EF, Frege, Resolution, or Cutting Planes has not reached NP != coNP unless a universal simulation theorem is added.
falsifier: assuming a p-optimal Cook-Reckhow proof system as an interface condition is invalid unless the route proves it or explicitly makes it a conditional target.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 4 converts proof-complexity enthusiasm into a precise bridge obligation: fixed-system lower bounds are extension-fragile. The P_tau construction is a concrete falsifier for the invalid inference from EF lower bounds to NP != coNP. This is valid route-level progress, not evidence for P != NP.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The current branch has not constructed an E-uniform explicit no-side MCSP selector with constant log-length gaps. Known density or counting facts do not identify valid tables without solving the meta-complexity problem or using nonuniform advice.
steps: Assume an explicit GapMCSP no-side carrier T_k at log-lengths n_k with C(T_k)>2^{epsilon n_k}.
For every target length r choose k=max{i:n_i<=r}; bounded gaps give n_k>r/gamma.
Define H on r-bit inputs by applying T_k to the first n_k bits and ignoring the suffix.
Uniformity of n_k and the bit generator for T_k puts H in E, since n_k<=r and evaluation costs 2^{O(r)}.
Any size-s circuit for H_r restricts, after fixing the ignored suffix, to a size s+O(r) circuit for T_k.
Thus s>2^{epsilon n_k}-O(r)>2^{delta r} for every delta<epsilon/gamma and all large r.
By IW, this conditional all-length E lower bound yields BPP=P; the route-level consequence is derandomization, not a proof of P != NP.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation is a conditional bridge from a strong carrier to derandomization. It neither proves that such MCSP carriers exist nor separates P from NP.

assumptions: Source model is GapMCSP on truth-table inputs of length N=2^n with no-side condition C(T)>N^epsilon.
The sequence n_k is increasing, computable from r in poly(r), and satisfies sup_k n_{k+1}/n_k<=gamma<infinity.
Each requested bit of T_k is computable in time 2^{O(n_k)}, or equivalently the full table is generated in E-uniform time 2^{O(n_k)}.
Target model is deterministic E and nonuniform Boolean circuits measured separately at each input length.
definitions: source object: an E-uniform sequence (T_k,n_k) of truth tables for n_k-bit Boolean functions, where T_k is a no-instance of GapMCSP_{*,N^epsilon}.
target object: a language H in E satisfying all-length circuit lower bounds CC(H_r)>2^{delta r} for some positive constant delta.
controlled interface: for each target length r, choose the largest source log-length n_k<=r and define H on r-bit inputs by evaluating T_k on the first n_k bits.
target-preserving condition: the source log-length gaps are bounded by a constant gamma and the hard-table selector is uniform, so delta<epsilon/gamma remains positive.

equations.label: mcsp_no_side_threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source carrier outputs GapMCSP no-instances at threshold N^epsilon with explicit log-length n_k.

equations.label: constant_gap_padding_window
equations.latex: n_k <= r < n_{k+1} <= gamma n_k implies n_k > r/gamma
equations.valid_when: Applies when every sufficiently large target length is padded from the previous source log-length.

equations.label: padded_language_definition
equations.valid_when: Valid when the selector k(r) is uniformly computable and ignored suffix bits are genuine padding.

equations.label: target_lower_bound_transfer
equations.valid_when: Requires constant gamma and any fixed delta below epsilon divided by gamma for all large r.

equations.label: iw_consequence
equations.latex: H in E and CC(H_r)>2^{delta r} for all large r implies BPP=P by IW
equations.valid_when: Requires the standard Impagliazzo-Wigderson theorem with uniform all-length exponential circuit hardness.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: if gamma is unbounded or the no-side table selector uses advice, the exponent delta is not valid for IW.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Conditional bridge lemma: it converts a named MCSP carrier with a quantitative gap invariant into the accepted E-hardness target for derandomization.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let GapMCSP have no-threshold t(N)=N^epsilon. If there is an E-uniform explicit sequence of no-side truth tables T_k of lengths N_k=2^{n_k}, with C(T_k)>N_k^epsilon and n_{k+1}/n_k<=gamma for a constant gamma, then there is H in E with all-length lower bound CC(H_r)>2^{delta r} for every fixed delta<epsilon/gamma. Hence the carrier gives the IW derandomization hypothesis, not P != NP.

assumptions: The only target construction is suffix padding of earlier truth tables.
The source gives no additional high-MCSP table in the interval (n_k,n_{k+1}).
Circuit lower bounds are measured as functions of the final padded input length r.
definitions: source gap ratio: g_k=n_{k+1}/n_k for consecutive available high-MCSP log-lengths.
induced exponent: delta_r=(log_2 lower_bound_at_r)/r when length r is filled by padding T_k.
threshold collapse: inf_r delta_r=0, so the IW all-length hardness premise fails.

equations.label: induced_padding_exponent
equations.latex: delta_r <= epsilon n_k/r for n_k <= r < n_{k+1}
equations.valid_when: Valid when padding preserves only the original T_k lower bound and adds no new hardness.

equations.label: collapse_at_right_endpoint
equations.valid_when: Applies near the next missing source length when the gap ratio g_k controls padding loss.

equations.label: no_iw_if_gaps_diverge
equations.valid_when: Requires infinitely many superconstant source gaps and no independent hard tables inside those gaps.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: exhibit only factorial, exponential, or otherwise superconstant gaps between explicit no-side MCSP tables.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Obstruction lemma: it certifies quantitative failure of the derandomization transfer under sparse carriers.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Sparse high-MCSP carriers with superconstant multiplicative gaps cannot be padded into an all-length 2^{Omega(r)} E lower bound by this interface; the induced exponent at target length r is at most epsilon n_k/r.

assumptions: Almost all truth tables have high circuit complexity, but this fact alone supplies no efficient index of one such table.
The target H must be a single uniform language in E, not a family of hard functions with advice.
definitions: selector: a function choosing one no-side truth table T_n for each source length n.
uniform selector: a selector whose bit relation BitSel(n,i)=T_n[i] is computable in 2^{O(n)} time.
leakage: dependence of T_n on nonuniform advice, oracle choices, or an uncomputable well-order of high-complexity tables.

equations.label: uniformity_condition
equations.latex: H(x)=T_{|x|}[x] is in E only if BitSel(n,i) is computable in 2^{O(n)}
equations.valid_when: Valid when translating a family of truth tables into one uniform target language.

equations.label: advice_failure
equations.latex: T_n chosen with a_n bits of advice gives H in E/a_n, not necessarily H in E
equations.valid_when: Applies when the hard-table choice is external to the uniform reduction or generator.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: the proof names hard tables only by existence or by a noncomputable lexicographic search over MCSP no-instances.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier-audit lemma: it separates real meta-complexity extraction from nonuniform leakage.
candidate_lemmas.statement: An existential counting argument for high-MCSP truth tables is not a valid carrier for E lower bounds unless the chosen hard tables have an E-uniform bit graph; otherwise the construction may encode arbitrary advice and the target language need not be in E.

control_decision.pivot_test: If every available MCSP/meta-complexity carrier has superconstant log-length gaps, vanishing threshold exponent, or only nonuniform hard-table selection, quarantine the IW-derandomization route and retain only sparse E lower-bound consequences.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote when a named source model supplies E-uniform no-side GapMCSP tables T_k with C(T_k)>N_k^epsilon and sup_k n_{k+1}/n_k<=gamma<infinity, yielding a checkable delta<epsilon/gamma transfer.
control_decision.reason: A valid conditional bridge was obtained, but the decisive missing object is now narrower: construct an explicit constant-gap no-side GapMCSP carrier without advice.

dependency_updates.description: Replace vague dense-carrier language by an explicit no-side GapMCSP sequence with threshold N^epsilon and constant multiplicative gaps in log-length.
Padding extraction from constant-gap high-MCSP tables to an all-length E lower bound is valid with exponent any delta<epsilon/gamma.
The selector for no-side tables must have an E-uniform bit graph; nonuniform selection is quarantined as leakage.
IW requires a fixed positive all-length exponent; sparse padding preserves it exactly when the source log-length gap is bounded by a constant.

The bridge itself is relativizing/combinatorial and does not evade P vs NP barriers; the missing source construction must be nonuniform-leakage-free and likely non-natural if it certifies many hard tables.

falsifier: the carrier selects high-MCSP tables by advice, oracle search, or counting, so the constructed target is nonuniform and not a valid E language.
falsifier: the MCSP reduction is length-balanced only on a sparse subsequence with superconstant gaps, giving sparse lower bounds but no IW all-length premise.
falsifier: the no-side threshold is t(N)=N^{epsilon(N)} with epsilon(N)->0, so even constant-gap padding yields no fixed positive delta.

falsifier: the source object is natural in the Razborov-Rudich sense, namely a large polynomial-time decidable useful property against circuits under standard PRF assumptions; the present single-sequence bridge avoids largeness, but a dense constructive proof may not.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 4 sharpens the route: rho-dense all-length carriers are sufficient but not necessary. A constant-gap explicit no-side MCSP sequence already transfers to all-length E hardness with exponent delta<epsilon/gamma. Conversely, superconstant gaps or epsilon(N)->0 create a quantitative threshold collapse, and nonuniform selectors invalidate the target class.
